'''Josef Biedermann''' (born 26 November 1944) is a former teacher and politician from [[Liechtenstein]] who served in the [[Landtag of Liechtenstein]] from 1978 to 1993. A member of the [[Progressive Citizens' Party]] (FBP), he served as the party's president from 1986 to 1987 and was the [[Vice President of the Landtag of Liechtenstein|vice president of the Landtag]] from 1989 to 1993.

== Life ==
Biedermann was born on 26 November 1944 in [[Feldkirch, Vorarlberg|Feldkirch]] as the son of teacher Franz Biedermann and Anny ([[Birth name|née]] Manahl) as one of eleven children. He attended [[Gymnasium (school)|gymnasiums]] in Feldkirch then [[Liechtensteinisches Gymnasium|Vaduz]] before studying secondary education and biology in [[Freiburg im Breisgau]]. From 1970 to 2008 he worked as a teacher of biology, chemistry, and biology at the [[Liechtensteinisches Gymnasium]], and was also its rector from 1987. Biedermann was a performer of  [[cabaret]] from 1964 to 1970.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=31 December 2011 |title=Biedermann, Josef |url=https://historisches-lexikon.li/Biedermann,_Josef |access-date=1 August 2026 |work=[[Historisches Lexikon des Fürstentums Liechtenstein]] |language=de}}</ref>

He was elected as a deputy member of the [[Landtag of Liechtenstein]] in the [[1974 Liechtenstein general election|1974 elections]] as a member of the [[Progressive Citizens' Party]] (FBP), and then as a full member in the [[1978 Liechtenstein general election|1978 elections]].<ref name=":0" /> During his time in the Landtag, he was a member of the body's finance, audit, foreign affairs, and provincial committees.<ref name=":0" /> Following the FBP's electoral defeat in the [[1986 Liechtenstein general election|1986 elections]], Biedermann served as acting president of the party from 1986 to 1987.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=26 November 2004 |title=Pflichtbewusst sein gegenüber dem Staat |url=https://www.eliechtensteinensia.li/viewer/!image/000476564_2004-11-26_20041126/8394/-/ |access-date=1 August 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Volksblatt]] |pages=4 |language=de}}</ref> In the [[1989 Liechtenstein general election|1989 elections]], he was the FBP's candidate for [[President of the Landtag of Liechtenstein|president of the Landtag]];<ref>{{Cite news |date=23 February 1989 |title=Wir stehen für eine ehrliche und saubere Politik |trans-title=We stand for honest and clean politics |url=https://www.eliechtensteinensia.li/viewer/!image/000476564_1989-02-23_19890223/651/-/ |access-date=24 August 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Volksblatt]] |pages=1 |language=de}}</ref> he was [[Vice President of the Landtag of Liechtenstein|vice president of the Landtag]] from 1989 to 1993.<ref name=":0" />

Biedermann was the FBP's candidate for [[Prime Minister of Liechtenstein]] in the [[October 1993 Liechtenstein general election|October 1993 elections]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=23 September 1993 |title=Josef Biedermann erhielt das Vertrauen der FBP-Delegierten am Parteitag |url=https://www.eliechtensteinensia.li/viewer/!image/000476564_1993-09-23_19930923/3269/-/ |access-date=20 July 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Volksblatt]] |pages=3 |language=de}}</ref> Originally intended to assume the position in the event of his removal as prime minister, he subsequently became the party nomination for the position once early elections had been called.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Meier |first=Günther |date=14 September 1993 |title=Parteien sehen keinen zwingenden Grund für sofortige Neuwahlen |url=https://www.eliechtensteinensia.li/viewer/!image/000476564_1993-09-14_19930914/3151/-/ |access-date=30 July 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Volksblatt]] |pages=1 |language=de}}</ref> The party lost the election to the [[Patriotic Union (Liechtenstein)|Patriotic Union]] (VU), and Biedermann resigned as a government candidate.<ref>{{Cite news |date=27 October 1993 |title=Verzicht auf Mitwirkung in neuer Regierung |url=https://www.eliechtensteinensia.li/viewer/image/000476564_1993-10-27_19931027/3785/ |access-date=31 July 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Volksblatt]] |pages=1 |language=de}}</ref> He was a member of the [[Planken municipal council]] from 2011 to 2019, and also the deputy mayor of the municipality.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=5 May 2015 |title=Weitere Vizevorsteher gewählt |url=https://www.vaterland.li/liechtenstein/gesellschaft/gemeinden/weitere-vizevorsteher-gewaehlt-art-129446 |access-date=1 August 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Vaterland]] |language=de}}</ref>

As of 2011, Biedermann has been a member of presidium at the  International Commission for the Protection of the Alps (CIPRA) since 1992.<ref name=":0" /> As of 2020, he has been the president Botanical-Zoological Society of Liechtenstein-Sargans-Werdenberg since 1995, and also president of the board of directors Adult Education Stein-Egerta from 1998 to 2016.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=31 December 2020 |title=Seit 50 Jahren im Einsatz für die Natur |url=https://www.vaterland.li/liechtenstein/gesellschaft/seit-50-jahren-im-einsatz-fuer-die-natur-art-440220 |access-date=1 August 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Vaterland]] |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2 December 2015 |title=Stabwechsel bei der Stein Egerta |url=https://www.vaterland.li/liechtenstein/gesellschaft/vermischtes/stabwechsel-bei-der-stein-egerta-art-171459 |access-date=1 August 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Vaterland]] |language=de}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Biedermann married [[Josephine Schöb|Josephine "Josy" Schöb]] on 6 April 1967 and they have three children together. Originally from [[Schellenberg]], he has been from [[Planken]] since 1997.<ref name=":0" /> His brother [[Franz Biedermann]] competed in the [[Athletics at the 1968 Summer Olympics – Men's decathlon|men's decathlon]] at the [[1968 Summer Olympics]], and his niece [[Katrin Eggenberger]] served as a government councillor from 2019 to 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stahl-Frick |first=Bettina |date=9 October 2020 |title=Raus aus dem Hosenanzug |url=https://www.vaterland.li/liechtenstein/politik/raus-aus-dem-hosenanzug-art-432476 |access-date=1 August 2026 |work=[[Liechtensteiner Vaterland]] |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=20 November 2024 |title=Katrin Eggenberger |url=https://historisches-lexikon.li/Eggenberger,_Katrin |accessdate=12 February 2026 |website=[[Historisches Lexikon des Fürstentums Liechtenstein]] |language=de}}</ref>
